name: American Community Survey 5-year Detailed Tables: commuting, vehicles, computers and internet
agency: U.S. Census Bureau
description: Survey-based 5-year period estimates with margins of error. Tables used here: B08301 means of transportation, B08303 travel time, B08012/B08013 aggregate travel time, B08014/B08201/B25044/B25046 vehicles available, B28001-B28003 computers and internet subscriptions.
access_requirements: None for table-based summary files (one pipe-delimited .dat per table, e.g. acsdt5y2024-b08301.dat); api.census.gov access is handled by the project adapter with a key
license: Public domain (U.S. federal government work)
update_cadence: Annual (2020-2024 table files dated 2026-01-29)
history_notes: 2019: B08301 transit sub-rows _011-_014 relabeled and reordered (e.g. _013 Subway became Long-distance train or commuter rail) and Worked at home became Worked from home; 2024: Taxicab relabeled Taxi or ride-hailing services; computer/internet items added 2013 and revised 2016 (caution comparing pre-2016).
suppression_rules: No suppression observed in sampled files; aggregate travel time rounded to nearest 5 minutes; block-group rows absent for B08013, B08014 and B08201 (tract is lowest level).
limitations: Sample survey with large MOEs for tracts and block groups; overlapping 5-year periods (compare non-overlapping periods); resident-based (where workers live); computer/internet items not asked of group quarters population.
doc_evidence: 2024 Subject Definitions: internet items added 2013, revised 2016; Taxicab label changed 2024. ACS20245YR_Table_Shells.txt and 2009-2023 API variable metadata confirm IDs/labels.
sample_evidence: Range reads of 2020-2024 b08301/b28002 .dat files: US drove alone 109,447,738 of 159,114,094 workers; broadband any type 117,573,073 of 129,227,496 households.

name: LEHD Origin-Destination Employment Statistics (LODES) version 8.4
agency: U.S. Census Bureau, Center for Economic Studies (LEHD program) with state partners
description: Job counts at 2020 census block level for workplaces (WAC), residences (RAC) and home-to-work pairs (OD) by job type, worker age, monthly earnings band and NAICS sector; race/ethnicity/education/sex from 2009; firm age/size from 2011 (JT02 only).
access_requirements: None. File patterns: {st}/wac/{st}_wac_{SEG}_{JT}_{YEAR}.csv.gz; {st}/rac/{st}_rac_{SEG}_{JT}_{YEAR}.csv.gz; {st}/od/{st}_od_{main|aux}_{JT}_{YEAR}.csv.gz; {st}_xwalk.csv.gz block crosswalk
license: Public-use Census Bureau data (U.S. federal government work); LEHD data page gives a requested citation format
geo_levels: state;county;cousub;place;tract;bg;zcta;cbsa;cd;sd;other:2020 census block (crosswalk also carries state legislative districts, tribal areas, workforce investment areas)
time_coverage: 2002-2023 for most states (data vintage 20251202). No OD/WAC files: AK 2017-2023, MI 2022-2023, MA 2002-2010, DC 2002-2009, AR and NH 2002, AZ and MS 2002-2003. Puerto Rico not included.
update_cadence: Annual (2023 data added December 2025)
history_notes: LODES8 uses 2020 blocks (LODES7 used 2010 blocks); federal (OPM) job types from 2010; worker demographics from 2009; job frame limited to ages 14-99 from 2012; earnings bands are fixed nominal thresholds ($1,250 and $3,333 per month).
suppression_rules: No cell suppression; Census disclosure avoidance review (CBDRB-FY21-249); state-years lacking employment data have RAC files only.
limitations: Counts jobs, not people (JT01 primary jobs approximates workers); administrative job frame (state UI records plus federal OPM), so self-employment is not covered; residence side partly modeled.
doc_evidence: Tech doc 8.4 (Rev. 20251203): OD/RAC/WAC at census block, years 2002-2023, state-year gap table (AK 2017+, MI 2022-23), file-name templates and variable lists.
sample_evidence: de_wac_S000_JT00_2023.csv.gz (175 KB): 7,383 blocks, 450,843 jobs (New Castle Co 298,174). Directory listings: AK WAC ends 2016, MI WAC ends 2021, MI RAC runs to 2023.

name: Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS)
agency: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, National Center for Statistics and Analysis
description: Census of fatal motor-vehicle crashes on trafficways open to the public (death within 30 days) with accident, vehicle, person and related files; crash location coded with GSA county and city codes and latitude/longitude (1999+).
access_requirements: None for static zip files; nhtsa.gov web pages and the CrashAPI returned HTTP 403 to scripted requests from this environment
license: U.S. federal government work (no copyright); no license terms found in files
time_coverage: 1975-2023 final files; 2024 Annual Report File (first release 2026-04-01)
update_cadence: Annual; the Annual Report File is replaced by a Final file about a year later
history_notes: COUNTY and CITY use GSA Geographic Location Codes (manual: codes occasionally divided); coordinates from 1999; data elements added and discontinued over time (documented in the Analytical User's Manual).
suppression_rules: None (census of qualifying crashes; no personal identifiers).
limitations: Location is where the crash occurred, not victims' residence; small annual counts in small counties (use multi-year sums); excludes non-fatal and non-trafficway crashes; manual covers Puerto Rico but the 2023 national CSV held 51 state codes.
doc_evidence: Manual DOT HS 813 794 (Apr 2026): census of fatal crashes, death within 30 days; COUNTY uses GSA codes; ARF later replaced by final file. Release notes: 2023 final file 2026-04-01.
sample_evidence: FARS2023NationalCSV.zip (34.2 MB): accident.csv 37,769 fatal crashes and 41,025 deaths across 51 state codes; person.csv 7,367 pedestrian and 1,163 bicyclist deaths.

name: FCC Broadband Data Collection (BDC) / National Broadband Map
agency: Federal Communications Commission
description: Provider-reported fixed broadband availability by Broadband Serviceable Location (technology, maximum advertised speeds, business/residential) and mobile coverage; Fixed Broadband Summary by Geography gives the share of BSL units served at 0.2/0.2, 10/1, 25/3, 100/20, 250/25 and 1000/100 Mbps by technology group.
access_requirements: Website downloads showed no login step (disclaimer only). Public Data API (bdc.fcc.gov/api/public/map/...) needs an FCC User Registration account and a generated token sent as username and hash_value headers; 10 calls per minute. fcc.gov hosts returned 403 to curl.
license: FCC public data; no explicit open license found; API token generation requires accepting FCC terms; Fabric location attributes (address, coordinates) are licensed via CostQuest and not public
geo_levels: nation;state;county;cd;place;cbsa;other:tribal areas;other:census block and H3 hexagon via location-level files
time_coverage: As-of dates 2022-06-30 through 2025-12-31, semiannual (8 vintages; data download page last updated 2026-09-15)
update_cadence: Semiannual (June 30 and December 31 as-of dates); earlier vintages revised after challenges (file names carry revision dates)
history_notes: Location-based BDC method (from June 2022) replaced Form 477 census-block reporting (last as of June 2021); the two series are not comparable. Location Fabric changes each filing round; summary-by-geography files restructured (spec v2.4.3, Aug 2026).
suppression_rules: None; public files identify locations only by Location ID.
limitations: Maximum advertised speeds reported by providers, not measured performance, price or adoption; satellite inflates any-technology coverage; values change as challenges are resolved.
doc_evidence: Download spec (Aug 11, 2026) defines summary files with share of units served per speed tier; API spec (Jun 8, 2026) requires account plus token; NBM page lists Jun 30, 2022-Dec 31, 2025.
sample_evidence: curl and WebFetch to broadbandmap.fcc.gov and fcc.gov returned 403; API needs registration; download page viewed in a browser (links present, nothing downloaded).

name: FCC Form 477 Fixed Broadband Deployment Data and Area Tables (legacy, to June 2021)
agency: Federal Communications Commission
description: Provider filings listing census blocks where fixed service is or could be offered (technology, maximum advertised speeds); Area Tables summarize population by number of fixed providers at speed tiers by geography with urban/rural and tribal splits.
access_requirements: None (Socrata SODA API; app token optional)
license: Public Domain U.S. Government (opendata.fcc.gov metadata)
time_coverage: Semiannual; opendata.fcc.gov holds block deployment files Dec 2015-Jun 2021 and Area Tables Dec 2016-Jun 2021 (earlier releases on fcc.gov not verified)
update_cadence: Discontinued (last data as of June 2021; superseded by BDC)
history_notes: Multiple versions per period (V1/V2); speed tiers 0.2 to 1000 Mbps; area tables use 2010 Census urban/rural and tribal flags; not comparable with BDC location-level data.
suppression_rules: None
limitations: A census block counts as served if a provider can serve at least one location in it, which overstates coverage; advertised speeds only; population-based coverage.
doc_evidence: opendata.fcc.gov jdr4-3q4p: fixed providers file lists of census blocks served for at least one location; data as of June 2021; newer data at broadbandmap.fcc.gov.
sample_evidence: SODA query of Area Table Jun 2021 (xvwq-qtaj): Kent Co DE, 25/3 fixed terrestrial (acfow): 4,354 of 183,641 residents with zero providers (97.6% covered).

name: NTIA Internet Use Survey (CPS Computer and Internet Use Supplement)
agency: National Telecommunications and Information Administration (fielded by the Census Bureau in the CPS)
description: CPS supplement on internet use by location, devices, household connection types and reasons for non-use; the NTIA Data Explorer file gives proportions and counts with standard errors for the U.S., demographic groups and each state.
access_requirements: None
license: Public domain (U.S. federal government work)
update_cadence: Irregular; November of odd years since 2017
history_notes: Questions and universes change across waves; some Explorer metrics are marked Legacy Metrics (No Longer Updated); universes include persons 3+, persons 15+ and households.
suppression_rules: None observed; SEs published for proportions and counts
limitations: State is the smallest geography; state SEs are about 1-2 percentage points; measures use, not availability.
doc_evidence: NTIA Data Explorer (June 06, 2024): Internet Use Survey data by state; categories Internet Use, Device Use, Household Connectivity; links ntia-analyze-table.csv.
sample_evidence: ntia-analyze-table.csv (2.3 MB, 835 rows, waves 1994-2023): Nov 2023 internet use, persons 3+: US 83.3%, Delaware 85.5% (SE 1.7 pts).

name: FBI Crime Data Explorer (UCR: SRS and NIBRS offenses, arrests, law enforcement employees)
agency: Federal Bureau of Investigation, CJIS Division, Uniform Crime Reporting Program
description: Agency-level offenses known to police (Summary Reporting System and incident-based NIBRS), clearances, arrests, law enforcement employees and participation; national/state estimates; bulk CSV and master-file downloads and a Crime Data API (JSON/CSV).
access_requirements: Free api.data.gov key (API returned 403 API_KEY_MISSING without a key); bulk files at https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/webapp/#/pages/downloads need no key
license: U.S. federal government work (public domain); FBI advises against ranking or comparing states or other entities except a city to its state and a state to the nation
time_coverage: Agency monthly series from 1985 (API); annual data through 2025 (released August 2026); NIBRS files by state and year
update_cadence: Annual release (August-September) plus monthly year-to-date master files
history_notes: SRS retired January 2021: 2021 data NIBRS-only with large gaps (CDE US population coverage averaged about 77% in 2021 vs about 96% in 2020 and 95% in 2022); NIBRS records all offenses in an incident while SRS used a hierarchy rule; estimation methods developed with BJS.
suppression_rules: No suppression of agency counts; UCR participation data identify partial reporters; national/state totals are estimated for non-reporting agencies.
limitations: Voluntary reporting of offenses known to police; agency jurisdictions do not match Census places; overlapping agencies (sheriffs, state police) complicate county totals.
doc_evidence: CDE API docs (browser): base api.usa.gov/crime/fbi/cde, link to get an API key, FBI advises against rankings; Downloads page: 2025 data provided August 2026.
sample_evidence: api.data.gov DEMO_KEY: Dover PD (DE0010100) 2023 violent offenses 381, property 2,192; 105 sworn officers; NY 2021 population coverage 68.9%; monthly data back to 1985.

name: UCR Program Data: County-Level Detailed Arrest and Offense Data (ICPSR/NACJD)
agency: FBI (producer); ICPSR National Archive of Criminal Justice Data (distributor, BJS-funded)
description: County aggregates of UCR Part I offenses and Part I/II arrests with ICPSR imputation for partial reporting, allocation of statewide agencies by population, and a county Coverage Indicator.
access_requirements: Free ICPSR sign-in and click-through Terms of Use; public-use files, no member-institution affiliation required
license: ICPSR Terms of Use: research or statistical use only; no redistribution without ICPSR written agreement
time_coverage: One ICPSR study per data year using the post-1994 method, 1994-2016 (latest ICPSR 37059 for 2016, V3 2019-01-17); no later year found
update_cadence: Irregular; no release after data year 2016 found
history_notes: 1994: new imputation algorithm and Coverage Indicator (not comparable with earlier county files); files are not official FBI UCR releases; 2016 V2 initially lacked adult and juvenile arrest parts.
suppression_rules: None; imputed values for agencies reporting fewer than 12 months.
limitations: Imputation can distort small counties; county level only; ends before the 2021 NIBRS transition.
doc_evidence: ICPSR 37059 page: county counts of Part I offenses and arrests; 1994 imputation algorithm and Coverage Indicator; public-use, membership not required.
sample_evidence: Download links require ICPSR login and Terms of Use acceptance; not attempted.

name: National Crime Victimization Survey (NCVS)
agency: Bureau of Justice Statistics (fielded by the Census Bureau)
description: Nationally representative household survey of persons 12+ on nonfatal personal and household property victimization, including crimes not reported to police.
access_requirements: None for published tables and dashboard; microdata distributed through ICPSR (terms apply)
license: U.S. federal government work for BJS products; microdata under ICPSR terms
update_cadence: Annual
history_notes: 2006 methodological changes may make that year non-comparable; decennial sample redesign in 2016; a redesigned instrument introduced in 2024 is to be reported separately.
limitations: National benchmark only; not designed for county or city estimates.
doc_evidence: BJS NCVS page: collection period 1973-2024; about 240,000 persons in 150,000 households; 2006 changes may make estimates not comparable.
sample_evidence: National-only product; no local rows relevant to sample for this catalog.

name: National Fire Incident Reporting System (NFIRS) Public Data Release
agency: FEMA U.S. Fire Administration
description: Incident-level reports from participating fire departments (fires, EMS, hazmat and other calls) in a relational database of about 20 tables; recent years also offered as geocoded GeoPackage files.
access_requirements: None; zip files 150 MB-3 GB (e.g. .../openfema/nfirs/nfirs_all_incident_pdr_{YEAR}.zip); fema.gov pages block some scripted clients
license: OpenFEMA Terms and Conditions: no re-identification; must state the product is not endorsed by FEMA; cite dataset, version and access date
time_coverage: 1980-2025: 1980-1998 fire incidents (NFIRS 4.1); 1999-2003 all incidents; 2004-2024 fire and hazmat; 2014-2024 all incidents; 2025 files dated 2026-06-03
update_cadence: Annual through data year 2025; NFIRS sunset February 2026 (replaced by NERIS)
history_notes: NFIRS 5.0 replaced 4.1 in 1999; 2025 was a hybrid NFIRS/NERIS reporting year; from 2026 incidents go only to NERIS (series break); participation varies by year and state.
suppression_rules: None documented for the PDR; OpenFEMA terms prohibit re-identification.
limitations: Voluntary, not a census; USFA says raw counts are not a proper measure of total fires, deaths, injuries or losses; department participation varies.
doc_evidence: USFA access page: PDR 1980-2024 on OpenFEMA, NFIRS 'not a census'; sunset page: 2026 incidents only in NERIS, NFIRS unavailable from February 2026.
sample_evidence: HEAD: nfirs_all_incident_pdr_2025.zip 1.34 GB (modified 2026-06-03), 2024 1.52 GB, fire_hazmat 2025 150 MB, GeoPackage 2025 3.0 GB; all above sample limit.

name: NEMSIS Public-Release Research Dataset (EMS activations)
agency: NHTSA Office of EMS / NEMSIS Technical Assistance Center
description: De-identified national file of EMS activations submitted by states to the National EMS Information System.
access_requirements: Request through a NEMSIS Help Desk ticket; a single year for the first request; NEMSIS terms of use
license: NEMSIS research dataset terms of use (not reviewed in detail)
time_coverage: 2025 dataset available (63,635,893 activations from 14,801 agencies in 54 states and territories); earlier years available by request (not enumerated)
update_cadence: Annual
suppression_rules: Public-release file has no patient, agency, hospital or reporting-state identifiers.
limitations: Cannot support local EMS metrics; state submission criteria vary and not all EMS events are submitted.
doc_evidence: NEMSIS page: 2025 PRRD has 63,635,893 activations from 14,801 agencies; file does not identify patients, agencies, hospitals or reporting states.
sample_evidence: Access by help-desk request; not attempted.

name: FEMA National Risk Index (v1.20, December 2025)
agency: Federal Emergency Management Agency
description: Natural-hazard risk for 18 hazards combining Expected Annual Loss with Social Vulnerability and Community Resilience; values, national percentile scores and ratings for composite risk and each hazard.
access_requirements: None (tract table NRI_Table_CensusTracts.zip is 635 MB); standalone NRI web application retired; data also in RAPT
license: FEMA NRI terms: must state the product uses NRI data but is not endorsed by FEMA; cite version and access date; no reverse engineering; FEMA may rescind use
time_coverage: Single cross-section v1.20 (December 2025; page updated January 6, 2026); hazard periods of record vary (e.g. hail 1986-2023, drought 2000-2025, hurricane 1851-2024)
update_cadence: Irregular versioned releases
history_notes: v1.20 overhauled inland flooding (pluvial plus fluvial) and tsunami and added USGS landslide data; Social Vulnerability now from Census Community Resilience Estimates; boundaries 2021 TIGER (Connecticut 2024); versions are not comparable.
suppression_rules: None
limitations: Planning-level screening; scores are percentile ranks among counties or tracts; do not compare across versions.
doc_evidence: FEMA NRI page: 'December 2025 v1.20'; application no longer available; data on OpenFEMA and RAPT. Metadata PDF: 18 hazards; SoVI from Census CRE.
sample_evidence: NRI_Table_Counties.zip (25 MB): 3,232 counties, 465 columns, NRI_VER December 2025; Kent Co DE RISK_SCORE 84.5 (Relatively Moderate), EAL_VALT $55.8M.

name: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database
agency: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (from NWS Storm Data)
description: Records of severe weather events with begin/end times, event type, direct and indirect deaths and injuries, and estimated property and crop damage by county or NWS forecast zone.
access_requirements: None. Pattern: StormEvents_details-ftp_v1.0_d{YEAR}_c{YYYYMMDD}.csv.gz (c = file creation date)
license: Public domain (U.S. federal government work)
time_coverage: 1950-present (current-year file d2026 created 2026-09-18)
update_cadence: Monthly updates to the current year; earlier years revised (creation date in file name changes)
history_notes: 1950-1954 tornadoes only; 1955-1992 tornado, thunderstorm wind and hail (1993-1995 only those three extracted); 55 event types since 1996 per NWS Directive 10-1605, a major break in 1996.
suppression_rules: None
limitations: Zone-based events need a zone-to-county correlation; damage estimates are rough, nominal and often missing; reporting practice varies by NWS office.
doc_evidence: NCEI app text: event types expand in 1955 and 1996 (55 types). Bulk CSV format PDF defines CZ_TYPE C/Z/M and damage strings such as 10.00K.
sample_evidence: StormEvents_details d2024 (12.7 MB): 69,801 events, 39,718 county-based (C) and 30,083 zone-based (Z); Delaware 83 events.

name: EPA AirData pre-generated annual AQI by county and CBSA
agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Air Quality System)
description: One record per county (or CBSA) per year: days with AQI, days in each AQI category, maximum, 90th percentile and median AQI, and days each pollutant was the main pollutant, from monitor data.
access_requirements: None; aqs.epa.gov reset scripted HTTPS connections from this environment (a browser loaded the page)
license: Public domain (U.S. federal government work)
time_coverage: 1980-2026 (2026 partial); all files as of 2026-06-25
update_cadence: Twice yearly (about June for the prior full year; about December for the ozone season)
history_notes: Area value is the highest among monitors; SO2 dropped from county/CBSA AQI summaries as of December 8, 2021; page posts a PM2.5 data advisory for recent files; monitor networks change over time.
suppression_rules: None; counties without monitors are absent.
limitations: Only about 1,000 counties per year (2024 file: 997 rows); days with AQI depends on sampling schedules; not population exposure.
doc_evidence: AirData download page (browser): files updated twice per year; annual_aqi_by_county files 1980-2026; 2024 file 997 rows, 20 KB, as of 2026-06-25.
sample_evidence: curl and Python requests to aqs.epa.gov were reset (ECONNRESET) from this environment; files not downloaded.

name: EPA EJScreen v2.3 (2024), archived copies (EPA tool removed February 2025)
agency: U.S. EPA (original producer); archived in Harvard Dataverse (HELD collection) and by Public Environmental Data Partners (PEDP)
description: Block-group and tract environmental burden indicators (PM2.5, ozone, NO2, diesel PM, air toxics, traffic proximity, lead paint, Superfund/RMP/TSDF proximity, USTs, wastewater, drinking water) with demographic, EJ and supplemental indexes and national and state percentiles.

license: CC0 1.0 per Harvard Dataverse record (EPA source data are U.S. government work)
time_coverage: Version 2.3 (2024 release; ACS 2018-2022 demographics); archived copy downloaded December 3, 2024
update_cadence: Discontinued (EPA public access ended February 5, 2025); no official updates

limitations: Screening tool, not a risk assessment; unofficial archived copies; PM2.5 tract values copied to every block group in the tract; percentiles are relative ranks.
doc_evidence: PEDP page: EPA public access 'discontinued on February 5, 2025'; epa.gov/ejscreen 404; Dataverse v4 (CC0) holds 2024 BG/tract CSVs and v2.3 tech doc (July 31, 2024).
sample_evidence: Range read of 20 KB of EJScreen_2024_Tract_with_AS_CNMI_GU_VI.csv (153 MB) via Dataverse API: tract 01001020100 ACSTOTPOP 1865, PM25 8.97.

name: CDC National Environmental Public Health Tracking Network: heat indicators
agency: CDC National Center for Environmental Health
description: Modeled historical temperature and heat index measures (extreme heat days and events for May-September and full year) for counties and census tracts, plus heat-related illness emergency department visits, hospitalizations and deaths.
access_requirements: No key required, but non-token requests are throttled (HTTP 429 observed); a free token is available by emailing trackingsupport@cdc.gov (per CDCgov/EPHTrackR README)
license: U.S. federal government work (no explicit license found)
time_coverage: Annual; available years not verified (API data calls throttled)

name: U.S. Drought Monitor county statistics
agency: National Drought Mitigation Center (University of Nebraska-Lincoln) with USDA, NOAA and NASA
description: Weekly percent of area (or population) in drought categories D0-D4 for counties, states and other areas, from the expert-blended U.S. Drought Monitor map.

license: No open license stated; USDM permission page asks reproductions to credit the partners and state 'Map courtesy of NDMC'

update_cadence: Weekly (map released Thursdays using data through Tuesday morning)

suppression_rules: None

doc_evidence: USDM web service page: CountyStatistics endpoint, 5-digit FIPS aoi, statisticsType 1 traditional / 2 categorical; What is the USDM: map released Thursdays.
sample_evidence: CountyStatistics aoi=10001 for 2024: 54 weekly rows (maps 2023-12-26 to 2024-12-31); 2024-12-31 Kent Co DE 100% of area in D2 or worse; earliest map returned 2000-01-04.

agency: U.S. Election Assistance Commission
description: Jurisdiction-level administrative data on registration, UOCAVA, mail voting, polling places and poll workers, provisional ballots and participation by voting mode.
access_requirements: None
